assumptions: Bilateral, symmetrical grip and movement on a flat bench with feet on the floor.
Joint actions describe the concentric press: elbow extension is the main driver, with glenohumeral horizontal adduction and flexion from the chest and anterior deltoid contributing.
Scapular protraction at lockout is a minor accompanying motion and is listed as assist.
The bar is held in the hands, so grip and wrist stability apply.
Back and hips are supported by the bench, so no postural or spinal stabilization demand is listed.
Elbows stay tucked, so the shoulder acts mainly as flexion and horizontal adduction with limited horizontal abduction demand.
classification_reasons: Flat bench barbell press with a close, roughly shoulder-width grip, performed bilaterally, is fully representable with the supplied vocabulary.
Instructions and contact sheet agree: the bar descends to the mid chest with the elbows tucked, then is pressed to lockout with emphasis on the triceps.

instructions: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close grip (around shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that - as opposed to a regular bench press - you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
